Event Details and Packing Checklist

Dear Parents and Learners,
We are delighted to announce the Children's Day Sleepover on Friday, 13 November 2026, which will also be a No-Bag Day.
Please note that 13 November 2026 will be a regular school day, and all learners are required to report to school in their regular school uniform. After school hours, learners will change into their comfortable clothing for the sleepover activities.
Please review the details and packing checklist below to help your child prepare for the event.

 

Sleepover Packing Checklist
We encourage children to carry a small suitcase or portable bag that they can manage independently. This will help them develop responsibility, confidence, and independence.

 

Please pack the following:
1. Rucksack / Small Suitcase (maximum total dimensions: 115 cm)
2. Comfortable clothes - 2 sets
3. Sweatshirt / Jacket - 1
4. Full-sleeved, full-length nightwear - 1 set
5. Hand towel - 1
6. Personal hygiene kit (toothbrush, toothpaste, face wash, comb, etc.)
7. Bedsheet - 1
8. Blanket / Quilt - 1
9. Pillow - 1
10. Floaters or comfortable footwear
11. Board games / UNO cards (optional)
12. Dry snacks

 

Important Reminders
1. Electronic gadgets such as mobile phones, iPads, smartwatches, and other devices are not permitted.
2. Prohibited items include sharp objects, scissors, cold drinks, aerated beverages, energy drinks, and chewing gum.
3. All belongings must be clearly labelled with your child's full name, grade and section.
4. If your child requires prescribed medication, kindly send email to infirmary with the details along with dosage instructions in advance.
5. Considering the weather, we recommend that learners carry mosquito repellent patches or cream.

 

Departure Arrangements – 14 November 2026
1. Dispersal will commence from 7:30 a.m. onwards on Saturday, 14 November 2026.
2.Parents of children who normally use school bus transport but wish to collect their child directly from school at 7:30 a.m. are requested to email us by 12 November 2026 (EOD).


We look forward to a memorable and enjoyable sleepover experience.

Dear Learners,

 

As discussed, please find below the details for your weekend project work, "Research and Make a Fossil."

Due Date for Submission: 12 Nov 2026

 

1. Research a Fossil

Choose one fossil and find out:

What was it?
Where was it found?
How old is it?
One interesting fact about it.

* Write your findings on an A4 sheet.

 

2. Write About Your Chosen Fossil

On the same A4 sheet, complete the following:

My fossil is: __________
It was found in: __________
It is approximately: __________ years old.
One interesting fact: __________
3. Make a Fossil Model
Use clay, dough, or any other suitable material.
Press a leaf, shell, toy, or another object into the material.
Carefully remove the object to create an impression.
Label your fossil model.

✨ You may research any fossil of your choice and create your fossil model using different materials or methods. Feel free to be creative!

 

Happy learning and fossil hunting! 🦴

Dear Learners,

Please note that your reading homework for today is uploaded under the 'Read and Reflect' module. 

How to access it:
Go to English Teams → go to the Classwork tab on the left side of your screen → open the "Read and Reflect" module.
Make sure to check this section every week and complete your weekly reading! 

 

This week's reading is the book Counting on Katherine: How Katherine Johnson saved Apollo 13

You've likely heard of the historic Apollo 13 moon landing. But do you know about the mathematical genius who made sure that Apollo 13 returned safely home? As a child, Katherine Johnson loved to count. She counted the steps on the road, the number of dishes and spoons she washed in the kitchen sink, everything! Boundless, curious, and excited by calculations, young Katherine longed to know as much as she could about math, about the universe. From Katherine's early beginnings as a gifted student to her heroic accomplishments as a prominent mathematician at NASA, this is the story of a groundbreaking American woman who not only calculated the course of moon landings but, in turn, saved lives and made enormous contributions to history.

 

Happy Reading!

What happens when the world's largest lizard comes face-to-face with one of the most venomous snakes? The mighty Komodo dragon has razor-sharp teeth, powerful claws and incredible strength, while the deadly king cobra has lightning-fast reflexes and a venomous bite. This fascinating nonfiction book compares their size, hunting skills, special abilities and defence mechanisms through exciting facts and colourful illustrations. When these two fearsome reptiles finally clash, only one can emerge victorious. Who will win this deadly battle? Read on to find out!

Dear Parents,

Greetings!

The Primary Humanitas Fest – HUMANVERSE 2026, held today, was a wonderful celebration of learning, creativity and collaboration across Grades 2–5. We are delighted to share that our learners put up an excellent showcase of their Humanities learning through their creative displays, models and presentations.

It was truly inspiring to witness our young learners take ownership of their learning and demonstrate student agency at every step. Their enthusiasm and confidence were evident as they shared their ideas, made decisions, explored different possibilities and worked together as a team. It was heartwarming to see how they listened to one another, built on each other's ideas, divided responsibilities and transformed their thoughts into meaningful projects.

Beyond the displays and presentations, what stood out was the learners' ability to think independently, collaborate purposefully, communicate their understanding and take pride in their work. Every effort reflected their curiosity, creativity, commitment and the joy of learning.

We would like to extend our heartfelt gratitude to all our parents for your encouragement, cooperation and support throughout the preparation for HUMANVERSE. Your involvement, motivation and willingness to support your children played a significant role in making this event a memorable experience. Thank you for giving our learners the confidence and encouragement to explore, create and express themselves.

The results of HUMANVERSE 2026 will be announced on 12 November 2026. We look forward to sharing the results with you!

As we celebrate the success of this event, we hope our learners carry forward the confidence, curiosity, teamwork and enthusiasm they demonstrated today into all their future learning experiences.

Thank you once again for being such an important part of our learning community and for helping us make HUMANVERSE 2026 a meaningful celebration of learning!

Warm regards,
Primary Humanities Team
